hook_segment.text: כולן מדברות על זה ואני סוף סוף הזמנתי...

causes_to_rate.a: Weak opening visual — flat catalog shot, no motion cue
causes_to_rate.c: AliExpress catalog feel — reads as a marketplace thumbnail, not organic TikTok
causes_to_rate.d: Generic hook text — no specific number/problem/surprise
causes_to_rate.e: Hook–product mismatch — text promises something the image doesn't show
causes_to_rate.h: Non-native Hebrew phrasing — grammatically valid but reads as translated/stilted

a.evidence: Same shared asset as the other three variants: 0s/1s frames show the identical static AliExpress hero-render (car phone mount + English badges), hard cut at 2s to the identical static AliExpress listing screenshot, held through 2.5s/3s. No motion within either half across the full 0-3s window -- confirmed the weakest-retention variant (25% at 2s) also has the least visual movement of any of them (tied with the others, since the asset is identical).

b.evidence: Product is clearly visible and labeled 'Vacuum Magnet' with feature badges at 0s, identical to A/B/C.

c.evidence: Identical shared asset: CGI-style AliExpress hero render with English badges (0-1.5s), hard cut to a literal AliExpress listing-page screenshot (2-3s). Same marketplace-thumbnail feel as every other 002 variant.

d.evidence: Hook text 'כולן מדברות על זה ואני סוף סוף הזמנתי...' ('Everyone's talking about it and I finally ordered...') is a highly generic FOMO/social-proof template with no specific number, no named problem, and no concrete surprise -- 'everyone's talking about it' names no source, no context, and no detail about what the product actually does. This is one of the most formulaic, product-agnostic hook openers possible.

e.evidence: Hook builds anticipation around social proof ('everyone's talking about it') and a personal purchase decision ('I finally ordered'), but the frames show neither social proof (no comments, no other creators, no crowd signal) nor an unboxing/ordering moment -- just the same static product render followed by an AliExpress price screenshot. The price screenshot arguably supports the 'I ordered' framing (justifying why), so it's a partial/loose match rather than a flat contradiction -- rated POSSIBLE rather than LIKELY.

h.evidence: 'כולן מדברות על זה ואני סוף סוף הזמנתי' is natural, colloquial spoken Hebrew and a very common authentic-sounding Israeli TikTok phrasing -- not stilted or translated. Note (outside this cause's definition): 'כולן' ('everyone', fem. plural) is again an explicit female-only address, matching the feminine-form pattern seen in 002A/B/C -- a gender-neutrality concern per the project's own copy rules, distinct from translation quality.

step11d_divergence_note: NO STEP 11D SCORE EXISTS FOR THIS PRODUCT -- same confirmed absence across all four 002 variants (output/2026-06-14-product-002-upload_package.md contains only a product-level 'STEP 3C: PASS', no per-variant STEP 11D verdict/score, unlike product 008's package which records one per variant). Nothing to diverge from for 002D specifically. Real-world result: WEAK retention, and the worst of the four (25% at 2s, n=315 views). Cross-variant pattern worth flagging: all four 002 variants (A/B/C/D) share the exact same 0-3s visual asset (static AliExpress product render -> hard cut -> static AliExpress listing screenshot); only the hook text changes. Retention across the four ranges narrowly from 25% to 39%, all WEAK -- consistent with a hook-text-driven (not visual-driven) difference layered on top of a uniformly weak, catalog-feeling creative that never had a STEP 11D check to catch it before launch.
